summary: Bumps the four exact-pinned CipherStash crates in protect-ffi (cipherstash-client, cts-common, stack-auth, stack-profile) from 0.42.0 to 0.42.2. The lockfile shows this also moves cipherstash-core/-config to 0.42.2, zerokms-protocol 0.12.26 -> 0.12.28, and jsonwebtoken 9.3.1 -> 10.4.0, swapping jsonwebtoken's crypto backend from ring to aws-lc-rs (already in the native graph via rustls, so native toolchain risk is low). No first-party code changes. The risk sits in upstream code that could not be read: a major-version JWT library change on the auth path that every ZeroKMS call depends on, a jsonwebtoken backend that may not compile for the shipped wasm32 entry, and opaque patch changes in the encryption/protocol crates. The Rust crates now differ from the @cipherstash/auth 0.42.0 npm catalog, which repo docs say should move together. The changeset is parked as .md.deferred, so the CVE fix does not reach published protect-ffi until the publishing cutover. Failures here would mostly be loud (build or auth errors), and the existing tests-rust and live integration-protect-ffi workflows are path-triggered by Cargo.lock, but no CI result was available.

behaviour_changes.description: Exact pins for cipherstash-client, cts-common, stack-auth and stack-profile move from =0.42.0 to =0.42.2. stack-auth, cipherstash-client and cts-common are unconditional dependencies, so they apply to both the native (Neon) and wasm32 builds.

Transitive jsonwebtoken (used by stack-auth) moves 9.3.1 -> 10.4.0, a semver-major change, and its crypto backend moves from ring to aws-lc-rs (plus signature, zeroize, getrandom). How stack-auth uses it (decode, validate, read exp for refresh) cannot be seen here.
Encryption and protocol crates also move: cipherstash-core and cipherstash-config 0.42.0 -> 0.42.2, and zerokms-protocol 0.12.26 -> 0.12.28. What these patches change is unknown.
A protect-ffi patch changeset is added as .md.deferred. Changesets ignores it, so no protect-ffi version bump or publish follows from this change until the cutover renames it.

The Rust CipherStash crates (0.42.2) no longer match the @cipherstash/auth npm catalog (0.42.0). dependabot.yml says these are one release train that should be bumped together, in step with the npm catalog.

failure_scenarios.title: jsonwebtoken 10 changes token handling in stack-auth, so ZeroKMS auth fails or tokens are mis-treated
failure_scenarios.trigger: Any encrypt/decrypt call that obtains a service token through AutoStrategy (access key, profile), a JS-backed @cipherstash/auth 0.42.0 strategy, or OIDC federation.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: stack-auth depends on jsonwebtoken, which moves a major version (9.3.1 -> 10.4.0) with stricter claim-type validation (the CVE fix) and a new crypto-provider model. protect-ffi turns every token into stack_auth::ServiceToken (lib.rs:815) and each ZeroKMS call goes through it. If stack-auth 0.42.2 decodes tokens or reads exp/nbf for refresh, a token that 9.x accepted, or a token minted by the 0.42.0 JS auth package, can be rejected or have its expiry misread. jsonwebtoken 10 may also fail at runtime if no crypto provider is selected on a target.
failure_scenarios.consequence: All encryption and decryption for affected consumers fails with auth errors after upgrade (an outage, loud). Or refresh mistimes and requests fail intermittently.

failure_scenarios.title: wasm32 build breaks because jsonwebtoken 10 now pulls in aws-lc-rs
failure_scenarios.trigger: Building protect-ffi for wasm32-unknown-unknown (tests-rust clippy, wasm-pack in build-ffi-binding and _build-ffi-artifacts).
failure_scenarios.mechanism: stack-auth is an unconditional dependency (Cargo.toml:26), so it is in the wasm32 graph. The locked jsonwebtoken 10.4.0 lists aws-lc-rs and no longer lists ring. aws-lc-sys builds C with cmake and does not generally target wasm32-unknown-unknown. If stack-auth enables jsonwebtoken's aws_lc_rs backend without a target gate, the wasm build fails. The lockfile cannot show target gating.
failure_scenarios.consequence: The ./wasm and ./wasm-inline entries cannot be built. This blocks CI and the next protect-ffi release and leaves edge-runtime consumers unable to upgrade. It is loud, not silent.

failure_scenarios.mitigation: Confirm the tests-rust wasm32 step and a wasm-pack build pass before merge. If they fail, the upstream crate needs a wasm-gated jsonwebtoken backend (for example rust_crypto on wasm32).

failure_scenarios.title: Opaque patch changes in cipherstash-client/core/config or zerokms-protocol alter ciphertext or protocol behaviour
failure_scenarios.trigger: Encrypting with the 0.42.2 crates and reading data written by 0.42.0 (or vice versa), or using search terms against installed EQL SQL.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: The change pulls in unreviewed upstream patch releases of the crates that produce encrypted payloads and talk to ZeroKMS (cipherstash-core, cipherstash-config, cipherstash-client 0.42.2, zerokms-protocol 0.12.28). The changeset asserts 'No API changes', but API stability does not establish payload or protocol stability, and none of the crate sources were visible.
failure_scenarios.consequence: If payload or search-term encoding shifted, values written at rest become undecryptable or unqueryable by older readers or SQL (silent, data-integrity).

failure_scenarios.mitigation: Read the upstream release notes for these patches. If they touch payload or term generation, add a fixture-based cross-version decrypt/query test.

failure_scenarios.title: Rust crates move to 0.42.2 while the @cipherstash/auth npm catalog stays at 0.42.0, leaving the CVE in the auth binding
failure_scenarios.trigger: Shipping stack/CLI with @cipherstash/auth 0.42.0 next to protect-ffi built on stack-auth 0.42.2.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: dependabot.yml records the four crates as the same release train as the @cipherstash/auth catalog and says to bump them together 'in step with the npm catalog'. pnpm-workspace.yaml still pins @cipherstash/auth and its six bindings at 0.42.0, and the dependabot comment still says =0.42.0. JS-backed strategies hand tokens and failure codes across this version boundary (lib.rs:617-655).
failure_scenarios.consequence: The CLI and stack auth binding probably keeps jsonwebtoken 9.x, so the advertised CVE remediation is partial. A cross-version token or error-code mismatch would degrade to AuthError::Custom or to auth failures.

evidence.claim: cipherstash-client, cts-common and stack-auth are pinned =0.42.2 under unconditional [dependencies]; stack-profile =0.42.2 only for non-wasm32.
jsonwebtoken locked at 10.4.0 with aws-lc-rs, signature, zeroize, getrandom; ring no longer a jsonwebtoken dependency.
aws-lc-rs 1.16.3 (and aws-lc-sys via cmake/cc) was already in the base lock, pulled by rustls; native builds already compile it.
zerokms-protocol moves 0.12.26 -> 0.12.28; the diff also moves cipherstash-core/-config/-client and cts-common to 0.42.2.
Deferred patch changeset for @cipherstash/protect-ffi describing the CVE-2026-25537 fix and asserting no API changes.
protect-ffi and its six platform packages are a fixed changeset group.
The four crates are the same release train as the @cipherstash/auth catalog, documented as =0.42.0, 'Bump them together, manually, in step with the npm catalog.'
@cipherstash/auth and six bindings remain pinned at 0.42.0; lockstep within that set is enforced by e2e/tests/supply-chain.e2e.test.ts.
JS-backed strategy failures are rebuilt via AuthError::from_error_code and tokens wrapped as stack_auth::ServiceToken on each get_token.
The wasm entry imports stack_auth AuthError, AuthStrategy, ServiceToken.
build:wasm runs wasm-pack for the crate; ./wasm and ./wasm-inline are published exports.
tests-rust is triggered on pull requests touching Cargo.lock and runs clippy for host and wasm32.
integration-protect-ffi (live ZeroKMS + Postgres, native and WASM) is triggered on pull requests touching Cargo.lock.
Integration tests exist for OIDC federation, JS strategy and lock context; results not seen.
